task: ae.shellx: bash-subset word expansion (quote lexing, brace lists/sequences, ${} operators, splitting) verified against real bash
reasoning_summary: Modelled each expansion stage as a pass over characters tagged with a quoting kind (plain, double-quoted, literal, splittable, marker), so later stages know what they may touch. A differential test against real bash (set -f) found four semantic gaps I had assumed away: brace digits extending a preceding $NAME, positional $1, a quote end terminating a name, and bash's rule that a } before any comma is ordinary text. A 15-mutant pass left one equivalent mutant, which was then removed by simplifying the code.
